note: Wording and anchors transcribed verbatim from the study's own CC BY S1 Appendix (incl. 'current recession' where other ACTS printings say 'recent', and the comma after 'run' the country); the appendix's parenthetical stats '(each item is 1=strongly disagree, 5=strongly agree; a=0.86, M=3.06, SD=1.02)' were dropped from instructions, and its endpoint anchors placed on resp 1 and 5 with 2-4 blank (no labels published). Direction confirmed: live person means give M=3.060, SD=1.021, alpha=0.856 against the published 3.06/1.02/0.86. Codes: data/enders_2022_conspiracy_vaccine.py keeps the Qualtrics column names CTSCALE_1..4; the deposit has no question-text row, no codebook, and .dta labels repeat the names, so nothing in the study's files ties a code to a statement. OVERRIDE OF THE SOURCE ORDER: the S1 Appendix lists 1 plots hatched, 2 few people run things, 3 not known to voters, 4 big events; the data reject that order. CTSCALE_1 has the highest agreement (57.4%) and lowest loading (.64), the signature of 'few people will always run things anyway' in every labelled sample (Kay & Slovic 2025 act_kay_2025: 70.5%/63.2% agree, loading .60/.71; Klofstad et al. 2019: lowest loading .66), while 'plots hatched' is the least-endorsed item in Kay (24.2%/27.0%). Scoring all 24 assignments against Kay's labelled columns (agree-% rank, loadings, 6 inter-item r) puts few/not known/big events/plots = CTSCALE_1..4 first (5.79 of 6) and the appendix order 9th (0.11). That order is also the one Uscinski et al. 2022 (PLOS ONE 17:e0270429, same authors) print in their main text, while their own SI prints the appendix order, so the SI listing looks like a documentation convention rather than the survey order. Shipped: CTSCALE_1 few people, 2 not known to voters, 3 big events, 4 plots hatched. 3 vs 4 is the weakest link (means 2.86 vs 2.75). Rights: instrument_rights_register.csv ACTS row (verdict ship, Ben 2026-09-23 irw#2381 R12, origin Klofstad et al. 2019 CC BY) applied, not re-derived; the wording here is the originating authors' own CC BY printing.
public_note: Item codes CTSCALE_1-4 are assigned to statements from the response data, not from the study's appendix, which lists the same four items in a different order (plots hatched first); the order shipped matches the item-agreement and correlation pattern of an independently labelled ACTS sample, with CTSCALE_3 vs CTSCALE_4 the least certain pair
